text: Which of the following molecule/species is most stable?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(B), the cyclopropenyl cation, is cyclic, planar and fully conjugated with $2π$ electrons, which fits $4n+2$ with $n=0$; it is aromatic and strongly stabilised.

(A) has only two $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ (cyclohexa-1,3-diene); its two $sp^{3}$ $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ groups break the cyclic conjugation, so it is non-aromatic. (C), the cyclopentadienyl cation, and (D), the cyclopropenyl anion, are cyclic, planar and conjugated with $4π$ electrons, so they are antiaromatic.

Aromatic stabilisation makes the cyclopropenyl cation the most stable species.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text: What happens to freezing point of benzene when small quantity of napthalene is added to benzene?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a small quantity of naphthalene is added to benzene, the freezing point of benzene decreases. This phenomenon is due to the colligative property known as freezing point depression. The addition of a solute, such as naphthalene, disrupts the orderly arrangement of solvent molecules in the solid phase, thereby lowering the freezing point.

Mathematically, the decrease in freezing point ($\Delta T_{f}$) can be represented by the equation:

$\Delta T_{f}=i\cdot K_{f}\cdot m$

where:

$i$ is the van't Hoff factor (which is 1 for naphthalene as it does not dissociate in solution),

$K_{f}$ is the cryoscopic constant of the solvent (benzene),

$m$ is the molality of the solution.

Thus, the correct option is:

Option B: Decreases
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Species)

(A) $\mathrm{Cr}^{+2}$

(B) $\mathrm{Mn}^{+}$

(C) $\mathrm{Ni}^{+2}$

(D) $\mathrm{V}^{+}$

List II (Electronic distribution)

(I) $3\mathrm{d}^{8}$

(II) $3\mathrm{d}^{3}4\mathrm{s}^{1}$

(III) $3\mathrm{d}^{4}$

(IV) $3\mathrm{d}^{5}4\mathrm{s}^{1}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Electrons are removed from the 4s orbital before the 3d orbitals.

$\mathrm{Cr}$ ($Z=24$): $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1}$, so $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{2+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{4}$, matching (III).

$\mathrm{Mn}$ ($Z=25$): $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{2}$, so $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1}$, matching (IV).

$\mathrm{Ni}$ ($Z=28$): $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{8}4s^{2}$, so $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{8}$, matching (I).

$\mathrm{V}$ ($Z=23$): $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{3}4s^{2}$, so $\mathrm{V}{}^{+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{3}4s^{1}$, matching (II).

The match is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I) : The orbitals having same energy are called as degenerate orbitals.

Statement (II) : In hydrogen atom, 3p and 3d orbitals are not degenerate orbitals.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Degenerate Orbitals: Orbitals that have the same energy are called degenerate orbitals.  

Hydrogen-like Atoms (Single-Electron Systems): In a hydrogen atom (or any one-electron system), the energy of an orbital depends only on the principal quantum number $n$, not on the azimuthal quantum number $l$. Therefore, all orbitals with the same $n$ (e.g., 3s, 3p, 3d) have the same energy and are degenerate.  

Multi-electron Atoms: In atoms with more than one electron, the energy also depends on $l$ (and other factors like screening), so 3s, 3p, and 3d orbitals are not all degenerate in multi-electron atoms.

Now, let us evaluate the given statements:

Statement (I): “The orbitals having same energy are called as degenerate orbitals.”  

This statement is true by definition.

Statement (II): “In hydrogen atom, 3p and 3d orbitals are not degenerate orbitals.”  

In a hydrogen atom, all orbitals with the same principal quantum number $n$ (like 3s, 3p, 3d) are degenerate.  

Hence, this statement is false.

Therefore, the correct option is:

Option A: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
Choose the correct statements from the following :

(A) Ethane-1, 2-diamine is a chelating ligand.

(B) Metallic aluminium is produced by electrolysis of aluminium oxide in presence of cryolite.

(C) Cyanide ion is used as ligand for leaching of silver.

(D) Phosphine acts as a ligand in Wilkinson catalyst.

(E) The stability constants of $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$ are similar with EDTA complexes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) Ethane-1,2-diamine binds a metal ion through both N atoms and forms a five-membered ring, so it is a chelating ligand: correct.

(B) Aluminium is obtained by electrolysis of $\mathrm{Al}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$ dissolved in molten cryolite, $\mathrm{Na}{}_{3}\mathrm{AlF}{}_{6}$ (Hall–Héroult process): correct.

(C) Silver is leached with dilute $\mathrm{NaCN}$ in the presence of air, the $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ ligand forming soluble $[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{2}]{}^{-}$: correct.

(D) Wilkinson catalyst is $[\mathrm{RhCl}(\mathrm{PPh}{}_{3}){}_{3}]$; its ligand is triphenylphosphine, $\mathrm{PPh}{}_{3}$, not phosphine, $\mathrm{PH}{}_{3}$: incorrect.

(E) The EDTA complexes of $\mathrm{Ca}{}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Mg}{}^{2+}$ have different stability constants ($\log K\approx 10.7$ and $8.7$), which is what allows their selective estimation in hard water: incorrect.

The correct statements are (A), (B) and (C) only.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
Following is a confirmatory test for aromatic primary amines. Identify reagent (A) and (B).


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the dye test for aromatic primary amines, the amine is first diazotised with $\mathrm{NaNO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{HCl}$ at 0–5 °C, which gives benzenediazonium chloride; so reagent (A) is $\mathrm{NaNO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{HCl}$ at 0–5 °C.

The diazonium salt is then added to β-naphthol (2-naphthol) in NaOH; coupling at C-1 gives 1-phenylazo-2-naphthol, the scarlet red dye that confirms the aromatic primary amine. So reagent (B) is β-naphthol.


[IMG]

α-Naphthol in option (C) also couples (at C-4), but the standard confirmatory dye test that gives the scarlet red dye uses β-naphthol.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : There is a considerable increase in covalent radius from $\mathrm{N}$ to $\mathrm{P}$. However from As to Bi only a small increase in covalent radius is observed.

Reason (R) : Covalent and ionic radii in a particular oxidation state increases down the group. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Covalent radius increases considerably from N to P, but only slightly from As to Bi. The heavier members contain completely filled $d$ and $f$ orbitals ($3d$ in As, $4d$ in Sb, $4f$ and $5d$ in Bi), which shield the outer electrons poorly; the higher effective nuclear charge offsets much of the effect of the added shell. Assertion (A) is true.

Down a group a new shell is added at each step, so covalent radii and ionic radii in a particular oxidation state increase. Reason (R) is true.

(R) gives only the general increase down the group; it does not account for the large rise from N to P and the small rise from As to Bi, which comes from the poor shielding by the filled $d$ and $f$ orbitals. So (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text: The compound formed by the reaction of ethanal with semicarbazide contains $_________$ number of nitrogen atoms.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ethanal condenses with semicarbazide: the free $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ group (the one not attached to $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$) adds to the carbonyl group and water is lost, giving ethanal semicarbazone.

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CHO}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

The product $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ contains three nitrogen atoms ($=\mathrm{N}{}^{-}$, $-\mathrm{NH}-$ and $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$).

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
$2\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}+\mathrm{bI}^{-}+\mathrm{cH}_{2}\mathrm{O}\to x\mathrm{I}_{2}+y\mathrm{MnO}_{2}+z\mathrm{OH}^{-}$

If the above equation is balanced with integer coefficients, the value of $z$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In basic medium Mn goes from +7 in $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}$ to +4 in $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}$ (gain of 3 electrons per Mn), and I goes from $-1$ in $\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$ to 0 in $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$ (loss of 1 electron per I).

Reduction half-reaction for 2 Mn, balanced with $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$:

$2~\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}+4\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}+6\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}+8\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$

Oxidation half-reaction supplying 6 electrons:

$6~\mathrm{I}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 3\mathrm{I}{}_{2}+6\mathrm{e}{}^{-}$

Adding the two halves:

$2~\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}+6\mathrm{I}{}^{-}+4\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow 3\mathrm{I}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}+8\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$

Check: O: $8+4=4+8$; H: $8=8$; charge: $-2-6=-8$. So $b=6$, $c=4$, $x=3$, $y=2$ and $z=8$.

Hence, the answer is 8.

[IMG]


An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic transformation starting from the point A and coming back to the same point by tracing the path $\mathrm{A}\to \mathrm{B}\to \mathrm{C}\to \mathrm{A}$ as shown in the diagram above. The total work done in the process is $__________ J$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the graph, A = (10 kPa, 10 dm${}^{3}$), B = (10 kPa, 30 dm${}^{3}$) and C = (30 kPa, 10 dm${}^{3}$). The work done on the gas is $w=-\int PdV$, and $1\text{kPa dm}^{3}=10^{3}\text{Pa}\times 10^{-3}\text{m}^{3}=1\text{J}$.

A $\to$ B is an expansion at constant $P=10$ kPa:

$w_{AB}=-(10\text{kPa})(30-10)\text{dm}^{3}=-200\text{J}$

B $\to$ C is a compression from 30 to 10 dm${}^{3}$ while $P$ rises linearly from 10 to 30 kPa, so the mean pressure is 20 kPa:

$w_{BC}=-(20\text{kPa})(10-30)\text{dm}^{3}=+400\text{J}$

C $\to$ A is at constant volume, so $w_{CA}=0$.

$w=-200+400+0=+200\text{J}$

The positive value means that net work is done on the gas in this cycle: the gas expands at low pressure and is compressed at higher pressure.

Hence, the answer is 200.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
The rate of a first order reaction is $0.04\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ at 10 minutes and $0.03\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ at 20 minutes after initiation. Half life of the reaction is $_______$ minutes.

 (Given $\log 2=0.3010,\log 3=0.4771$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given values are rates (unit $\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$), not rate constants. For a first order reaction, rate $=k[\mathrm{A}]$, so the ratio of rates equals the ratio of concentrations:

$\dfrac{[\mathrm{A}]_{10}}{[\mathrm{A}]_{20}}=\dfrac{0.04}{0.03}=\dfrac{4}{3}$

Over the interval from 10 min to 20 min ($\Delta t=10$ min), the first order rate law gives

$k=\dfrac{2.303}{10}\log \dfrac{4}{3}\text{\min }^{-1}$

$\log \dfrac{4}{3}=2\log 2-\log 3=0.6020-0.4771=0.1249$

$t_{1/2}=\dfrac{2.303\log 2}{k}=\dfrac{10\log 2}{\log (4/3)}=\dfrac{10\times 0.3010}{0.1249}\approx 24.1\text{\min }$

Hence, the answer is 24.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text: On a thin layer chromatographic plate, an organic compound moved by $3.5\mathrm{cm}$, while the solvent moved by $5\mathrm{cm}$. The retardation factor of the organic compound is $________$ $\times 10^{-1}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Retardation factor $=\frac{\text{Distance travelled by sample/organic compound}}{\text{Distance travelled by solvent}}$

$=\frac{3.5}{5}=7\times 10^{-1}$

text: If IUPAC name of an element is "Unununnium" then the element belongs to $n^{th}$ group of Periodic table. The value of n is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In IUPAC systematic names each digit of the atomic number has a root (un $=1$) and the name ends in -ium, so un-un-un-ium (printed here as Unununnium) stands for atomic number 111, the element now named roentgenium (Rg).

Period 7 begins with Fr (87, group 1) and Ra (88, group 2); Ac (89) and the actinoids up to Lr (103) are placed in group 3, and the $6d$ series continues with Rf (104) in group 4.

Counting on, 105 is in group 5, 106 in group 6, and so on, so element 111 is in group 11, below Cu, Ag and Au.

So $n$, the group number, is 11, while 111 is the atomic number.

Hence, the answer is 11.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift
